events.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Lukoil Volgograd refinery
events.capacity_units_note: Source gives '~300,000 bpd (14.5 million tons/year)'. Recorded as 300 kb/d; the source's own tilde is preserved in the quote.

unknown_reasons.capacity_affected_kbd: NO SOURCE ATTRIBUTES AN OUTAGE TO THIS EVENT. The contemporaneous report (Kyiv Independent, 2025-01-31) says only that 'the extent of the damage is still being assessed'. The halt and restart widely reported in February 2025 are attributed by their own source (Hydrocarbon Processing, 2025-02-12) to a SEPARATE strike on 3 February 2025 -- 'Ukrainian drone attack on February 3' -- and that article does not mention the 31 January strike at all. Carrying the February outage onto this event would be inference from a neighbouring event, which EXPOSURE_REGISTRATION §2 forbids by name.
unknown_reasons.days_to_partial_restore: Same: the 10 February CDU-5 restart belongs to the 3 February strike.

events.title: Ukrainian drone strike on CPC Kropotkinskaya pumping station
events.asset_name: Kropotkinskaya oil pumping station, Caspian Pipeline Consortium (Tengiz-Novorossiysk system)
events.capacity_units_note: Nameplate NOT recorded. The only throughput figure found is in tonnes: 'In 2024, the pipeline loaded more than 63 million tons of oil onto tankers at Novorossiysk terminal annually' (The Moscow Times, 2025-02-17). Converting tonnes/year to kb/d requires a crude-density assumption, which would be an unsourced inference, so no kb/d value is entered.

days_to_partial_restore.quote: Oil transportation through the Tengiz-Novorossiysk pipeline system is being carried out at reduced pumping levels -- reported the same day as the strike, so flows were never fully stopped and first material resumption is 0 days.

days_to_full_restore.quote: Relaunched in technological pumping mode after restoration work and currently operating in normal oil-pumping mode. 2025-02-17 to 2025-05-23 = 95 days.

unknown_reasons.capacity_nameplate_kbd: Only a tonnes-per-year throughput figure is available; no kb/d source found. See capacity_units_note.
unknown_reasons.capacity_affected_kbd: Transneft projected that 'the volume of oil pumped from Kazakhstan could decrease by approximately 30%' (Interfax, 2025-05-23). That is a projected PERCENTAGE, explicitly approximate, and applying it to a tonnes-based throughput would compound two unsourced steps. No kb/d value entered.

events.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Rosneft Novokuibyshevsk refinery
events.capacity_units_note: Nameplate NOT recorded. The only figure in the contemporaneous report is 'an annual capacity of up to 8.8 million metric tons', attributed to Ukraine's National Security and Defence Council spokesman -- tonnes, 'up to', and a belligerent's claim rather than an operator or agency figure.

unknown_reasons.capacity_nameplate_kbd: See capacity_units_note: tonnes only, 'up to', and sourced to a claim.
unknown_reasons.capacity_affected_kbd: No outage is established for this event. The regional governor called the strike 'a failure' with no damages while the Emergency Situations Ministry reported a fire; the article states no halt. The complete shutdown widely reported for this refinery belongs to a SEPARATE strike on 2 August 2025.
unknown_reasons.days_to_partial_restore: No halt established for this event, so no restoration to measure.

events.title: Houthis resume Red Sea attacks sinking Magic Seas
events.asset_name: Bab el-Mandeb Strait / southern Red Sea transit route
events.capacity_units_note: Prevailing oil trade flow at the time of the event, not a physical capacity: a chokepoint has throughput, not nameplate. The 2023 full-year figure of 8.7 mb/d is given in the same source and is the pre-Houthi-disruption level.

capacity_nameplate_kbd.quote: Oil trade flows through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait averaged 4.0 million barrels per day (b/d) in 2024 through August compared with 8.7 million b/d in full-year 2023

unknown_reasons.capacity_affected_kbd: No source found quantifying, in barrels, the flow removed by the 6 July 2025 resumption of attacks. Transit-count changes are reported but converting a vessel count to a barrel volume is an unsourced inference.
unknown_reasons.days_to_partial_restore: Not established: the route was already operating at roughly half its 2023 flow before this event, so there is no pre-event baseline to restore TO that a source states.

events.title: Codelco El Teniente collapse 2025
events.capacity_units_note: OUT OF UNIT SCOPE. This is a COPPER MINE. asset_type has no admissible value (the enum is refinery/terminal/field/pipeline/chokepoint/processing/storage) and capacity in kb/d is undefined for it -- copper capacity is tonnes of ore or refined metal. Every kb/d field is left unknown BY CONSTRUCTION, not for want of research: entering any number here would be a category error, not a sourcing gap. Flagged to Joe: EXPOSURE_REGISTRATION §1 scopes the layer to the 75 physical-asset events by CLASS, and this event's class is infrastructure_attack, so a non-petroleum asset is inside the registered scope while outside the schema's units.

unknown_reasons.capacity_nameplate_kbd: Copper mine: kb/d is not a unit this asset has.

events.title: Ukrainian drone strike halts Rosneft Saratov refinery
events.capacity_units_note: Nameplate NOT recorded, and SOURCES DISAGREE. The Moscow Times (2025-08-11) gives 'an annual processing capacity of 5.8 million metric tons'; other reporting gives 4.8 million t/y and 140,000 bpd. Both are tonnes-based or unverified, they conflict, and no conversion is made.

unknown_reasons.capacity_affected_kbd: The source establishes that the refinery 'halt[ed] crude intake' but gives no volume.
unknown_reasons.days_to_partial_restore: No restart date found in any source for this strike.
unknown_reasons.date_note: The Moscow Times (2025-08-11) reports the halt as occurring 'on Sunday', i.e. 2025-08-10, while the corpus dates this event 2025-08-11. Reported, not corrected -- the corpus is not this session's file.

events.title: Ukrainian strike halts Druzhba pipeline oil flow to Hungary and Slovakia
events.asset_name: Druzhba pipeline -- Nikolskoye pumping station (Tambov region), southern branch to Hungary and Slovakia
events.capacity_units_note: No capacity figure found in any fetched source for the Druzhba southern branch or for deliveries to Hungary and Slovakia.

days_to_partial_restore.quote: UPPER BOUND FROM TWO SOURCED DATES, stated as such. Flows halted 2025-08-18 (The Moscow Times, 2025-08-18). The resumption report is published 2025-08-20 and says flows 'resumed Tuesday evening'; 19 August 2025 was a Tuesday, so the actual resumption was 1 or 2 days after the halt. 2 is the date by which the source reports resumption; it is not narrowed further because the article's own wording does not settle it.

days_to_full_restore.quote: Slovak Economy Minister Denisa Sakova: 'The flow of oil to Slovakia is currently standard' -- i.e. pre-event capacity restored by 2025-08-20, 2 days after the 2025-08-18 halt. Same upper-bound caveat as above.

unknown_reasons.capacity_affected_kbd: Sources state deliveries to Hungary and Slovakia were halted but give no volume.
unknown_reasons.operator: Not stated in the fetched sources. Transneft operates Druzhba but no fetched source says so for this station, so it is left unknown rather than filled from general knowledge.

events.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Rosneft Ryazan refinery
events.capacity_units_note: Source says 'more than 260,000 barrels per day'; recorded as 260 kb/d, i.e. the source's floor. The contemporaneous report (The Moscow Times, 2025-09-05) gives only a tonnes range, 'between 13.7 million and 17.1 million tons of crude annually', which is not converted.

capacity_nameplate_kbd.quote: more than 260,000 barrels per day of crude-or 5% of Russia's refining capacity

unknown_reasons.capacity_affected_kbd: NOT QUANTIFIED FOR THIS STRIKE. The contemporaneous source gives no figure for the 5 September impact. The widely-cited '80,000 bpd offline, about a quarter of total capacity' belongs by its own source (OilPrice.com, 2025-11-18) to an OCTOBER strike, and the ~50% cut belongs to an early-August one. Ryazan was struck at least nine times in 2025; attributing another strike's outage here is exactly the inference §2 forbids.
unknown_reasons.days_to_partial_restore: Same: the 'idle until the end of the month, no loadings before December 1' figure belongs to the November strike.

events.title: Ukrainian drone strike halts oil loadings at Novorossiysk Sheskharis terminal
events.capacity_units_note: Nameplate is the terminal's normal crude loading volume: Kpler gives Sheskharis as '36%, around 830 kbd' of Novorossiysk's 2.3 Mb/d. Affected is the volume Kpler states was halted (~700 kbd of Urals, KEBCO and SBL).
events.downstream_dependency: Crude exports to India and Turkey (Urals, KEBCO, SBL grades) per Kpler, 2025-11-18

capacity_nameplate_kbd.quote: 36%, around 830 kbd (Sheskharis share of Novorossiysk's 2.3 Mb/d)

capacity_affected_kbd.quote: removing ~700 kbd of Urals, KEBCO and SBL supply, mainly to India and Turkey

days_to_partial_restore.quote: On Sunday, Reuters reported that Novorossiysk had resumed oil loadings, with two tankers loading crude at the port's terminals at the time. Strike 2025-11-14, resumption Sunday 2025-11-16 = 2 days.

days_to_full_restore.quote: Kazakhstan's Energy Minister said 'all operations' at the Sheskharis oil transshipment complex were restored on Monday 2025-11-17 = 3 days.

unknown_reasons.operator: Not stated in the fetched sources; left unknown rather than filled from general knowledge.

events.title: Iran declares the Strait of Hormuz closed
events.capacity_units_note: Nameplate is the pre-event oil flow through the strait, from a source published BEFORE the event (EIA, 2025-06-16), so it is not retrospective. Affected is the IEA's own figure for exports disrupted: the source's word is 'nearly 20 mb/d', preserved verbatim in the provenance quote.
events.alt_routing_available: Partial: Saudi East-West pipeline to the Red Sea and the UAE's 1.8 million b/d pipeline to Fujairah (EIA, 2025-06-16). IEA (2026-03-12) states 'limited capacity available to bypass the crucial waterway'.
events.source_publisher: International Energy Agency, Oil Market Report

capacity_nameplate_kbd.quote: In 2024, oil flow through the strait averaged 20 million barrels per day (b/d), or the equivalent of about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption.

capacity_affected_kbd.source_publisher: International Energy Agency, Oil Market Report
capacity_affected_kbd.quote: With nearly 20 mb/d of crude and product exports currently disrupted and limited alternative options to bypass the world's most critical oil transit chokepoint, producers and consumers globally are feeling the strain.

days_to_partial_restore.quote: Five vessels crossed the strait on Wednesday (2026-04-08), seven on Thursday, after the US-Iran ceasefire; the route typically handled about 120-140 daily transits before the attacks of 28 February. First transits 2026-04-08, event 2026-03-04 = 35 days.

days_to_full_restore.quote: ONGOING as of the stamp date 2026-08-05, permitted by §2. 'Preliminary data show 84 transits during 27 July to 2 August, up from 45 the previous week' -- about 12 a day against a pre-crisis 120-140 a day, so pre-event capacity has NOT been restored.

block_note: Filled by Session K, 2026-09-03, under EXPOSURE_REGISTRATION.md §2 (commit 22da52f). Every numeric carries per-field provenance in `provenance`; every unknown carries its reason in `unknown_reasons`. No figure is estimated, interpolated or carried across from a neighbouring event. Three events were struck more than once in the period and their widely-reported outage figures belong to a DIFFERENT strike than the one dated here (Volgograd, Novokuibyshevsk, Ryazan); those fields are left unknown with the attribution named, which is the main reason this block has 2 COMPLETE and not 5.
